findings.title: Action-norm-scaled confidence intervals are invalid for the stated bounded scalar noise
findings.assumptions: n=1, theta=1, A={.001,.002,.003}, K=3,T=1000,D=1; independent Bernoulli(a) payoffs; S=A, coordinate representations, epsilon=0
findings.decisive_evidence: First epoch has two pulls per arm. Exactly one success on arm .001 and all other rewards zero has probability .001978093806191928. LCB optimal=.49532861068571515 exceeds UCB arm .002=.009342778628569665; B=1. The confidence failure exceeds 2/T^2. All original domain/noise/spanner assumptions hold.
findings.alternative_readings: Unit-norm actions in Section 5 avoid this counterexample but the stated domain is the unit ball. Norm-scaled noise would be a stronger unstated model. Equations (32)-(33) actually include absolute coefficients; OCR candidate rejected.
findings.core_dependency: Valid UCB/LCB -> retention Lemma A.3 -> regret Lemmas A.4-A.6 -> A.1/3.3 -> contextual Theorem4.1; reward proof also reuses confidence event.
findings.impact: Demonstrated core proof/algorithm confidence failure, not a numeric refutation of the big-O regret bound on this finite instance.
findings.correction: For bounded scalar noise use beta/sqrt(q), not beta*norm(a)/sqrt(q), and absolute-coefficient propagation; this local concentration repair is supported, full regret proof not certified.

findings.title: Reward guarantee proof replaces the implemented maximum of UCBs by a minimum
findings.assumptions: Two component upper confidence bounds; epsilon=0 suffices; comparison conditional on their validity, independently of P1.
findings.decisive_evidence: Algorithm defines max(UCB1,UCB2). B.3 explicitly asserts min and uses UCB<=UCB2. B.4 infers UCB1>=B from survival, which max does not imply. Example UCB1=.8,UCB2=.6 makes the B.3 comparison false algebraically; illustrative values are not claimed to be a full trajectory counterexample.
findings.alternative_readings: A one-word transcription error is plausible. A maximum is still an upper bound, so optimal-arm optimism alone is not refuted. Slower elimination might admit a different analysis.
findings.core_dependency: B.3 and B.4/B.5 are directly combined in Theorem B.1 for advertised reward guarantees and loss/reward comparison.
findings.impact: As-written derivation proves a different rule; no demonstrated impossibility of the reward rates or empirical failure.
findings.correction: Using min preserves optimism if each component is valid and supplies both inequalities; this local algebraic repair is verified, full repaired theorem not verified.

needs_evidence: Early-epoch summation on p18 needs an explicit action-count argument: a complete epoch contains 3n*2^m pulls; displayed discarded block uses 2^m Delta_max. No additional supported severity assigned.
Contextual proof p26 transfers instance-dependent gaps from empirical reduced actions to population gaps without detailed perturbation handling; not independently certified.
Zero-complete-observation conventions, terminal partial epochs and logarithm floors need explicit specification.
No author repository/seed outputs available in supplied manifest; empirical claims not reproduced. Experiments intentionally omit guess B and use unit-norm actions.
